title: NEB Class 12 Chemistry — Chemical Kinetics — 2021
origin: curated NEB-pattern set for class-12 chemical kinetics

questions.question: Define rate of reaction, rate law, order and molecularity. For the reaction $2\mathrm{N_2O_5 \rightarrow 4NO_2 + O_2}$ with rate $= k[\mathrm{N_2O_5}]$, state the order and molecularity.
questions.solution:
Rate is the change in concentration per unit time. The rate law is the experimentally found expression rate $= k[A]^m[B]^n$. Order ($m+n$) is found by experiment; molecularity is the number of species colliding in one elementary step (a theoretical whole number).
Here the rate depends on $[\mathrm{N_2O_5}]$ to the first power, so the order is 1 (first order). The balanced equation consumes 2 molecules, but the slow (rate-determining) step is $\mathrm{N_2O_5 \rightarrow}$ products — unimolecular, so molecularity is 1. Order is experimental, molecularity is mechanistic: they need not match.

questions.question: Derive the integrated rate equation for a first-order reaction and show that its half-life is independent of initial concentration. A first-order reaction is 75% complete in $60$ minutes — find its half-life.
questions.solution:
First order: $-d[A]/dt = k[A]$. Separating and integrating from $[A]_0$ to $[A]$: $\ln([A]_0/[A]) = kt$, or $[A] = [A]_0 e^{-kt}$.
Half-life: $[A] = [A]_0/2$ gives $t_{1/2} = \ln 2/k$ — no $[A]_0$ appears, so half-life is concentration-independent.
75% complete means $[A] = 0.25[A]_0$: $k = \ln(1/0.25)/60 = \ln 4/60 = 2\ln 2/60$. Then $t_{1/2} = \ln 2/k = 60/2 = 30$ minutes.

questions.question: The activation energy of a reaction is $E_a$. A catalyst provides an alternative path with lower $E_a$. What happens to the rate constant $k$, and does the catalyst change the equilibrium constant?
questions.solution: By Arrhenius $k = Ae^{-E_a/RT}$, lowering $E_a$ increases the fraction of successful collisions, so $k$ increases (reaction speeds up). The catalyst lowers the barrier for forward AND reverse reactions equally, so it reaches equilibrium faster but the equilibrium constant $K$ — fixed by thermodynamics ($\Delta G^\circ$) — is unchanged.
